data.long_meaning: Shik is a Hindi and Sanskrit name derived from the Sanskrit word 'shiksha', which means 'learning'. It symbolizes intelligence, knowledge, and the pursuit of wisdom. It is an excellent name for a child destined to excel academically or in any intellectual pursuit. The name Shik carries the meaning “Learning, Wisdom” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Shik usually hope their child will grow to embody learning, wisdom and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Shik represents the quest for knowledge and wisdom in the spiritual realm. It is a reminder to continually seek enlightenment and understanding, both of oneself and the world around us.
data.etymology: Shik belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Learning, Wisdom.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shik total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

historical_references.reference: Shikharshila was a renowned Hindu religious site located in the present-day state of Bihar, India. It is believed that the site was a major center of learning and scholarship during the Gupta Empire (c. 320-550 CE). The name 'Shik' in the site's name is believed to be derived from the Sanskrit word 'shikhara', meaning 'peak' or 'summit'. This reference highlights the historical significance of the name 'Shik' in relation to a major Hindu religious and learning center during the Gupta Empire.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to the name 'Shik' can be found in the Hindu epic 'Mahabharata'. In the epic, 'Shikhandi' is a character who is a transgendered warrior. This reference highlights the historical significance of the name 'Shik' in relation to a transgendered character in Hindu mythology.
